data.title: Trump says wind turbine part imports cause national security issue, but doesn't impose tariffs
data.description:
The Trump administration has determined that imports of wind turbine parts pose a national security threat, but it does not appear to be opting to tariff them.

President Trump issued a memo on Thursday saying that “wind turbines and their components and subcomponents are being imported into the United States under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States.”

But the memo stopped short of saying there should be tariffs on imported wind turbines. Instead, it said that the U.S. should negotiate with trading partners to “adjust” imports of wind turbines and their components. 

Trump has been a longtime critic of wind energy and has particularly decried turbines as ugly. His administration has put up a number of hurdles for the buildout of renewable energy broadly and wind in particular, including claims that they could interfere with national security and radars.

Wind supporters have criticized such claims as a pretext to block an energy source the president simply does not like. 

Trump’s latest memo says that wind turbines containing foreign-made parts may “contain cybersecurity vulnerabilities that could lead to remote control access to wind turbines and cause power disruption.”

It also criticized wind more broadly as an “unreliable and intermittent energy source.”

data.title: Trump on the Alaska election lawsuit: 'I'm the one that said, "do it"'
data.description:
President Trump said Friday he directed the Department of Justice (DOJ) to file a lawsuit to block certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses in November. 

DOJ filed the suit Thursday, claiming that the existence of a candidate with a similar name to Sullivan would make a win by Democrat Mary Peltola invalid. Trump told reporters upon arriving in Florida that he had greenlit the preemptive election challenge himself. 

“I’m the one who said ‘do it,’” Trump said. 

The issue stems from Dan J. Sullivan Jr., who is running for Senate in Alaska and will — after extensive litigation that reached the state Supreme Court — appear on the November ballot against an incumbent senator with nearly the same name.

The DOJ said Sullivan Jr. is running with the intention of confusing voters and asked a judge to block the certification of the election if the incumbent loses in a scenario where if all the votes cast for Sullivan Jr. had gone to the incumbent, he would have won.

In Alaska, the top four vote getters in the primary advance to the general election, which is tabulated using ranked-choice voting. While they have similar names, the two Sullivans will appear differently on the ballot, with the senator labeled “incumbent” and “Republican.”

The incumbent Sullivan’s campaign spokesperson, Nate Adams, told The Hill that the campaign will let the DOJ challenge run its course and that Alaskans will be able to differentiate between the two Sullivans based on their records.

Trump has claimed that Democrats recruited Sullivan Jr. to run against Peltola and the incumbent Sullivan in a race that could decide control of the Senate. Many Republicans, including the incumbent, have theorized that Sullivan Jr.’s campaign is a Democratic ploy to confuse voters and cause a Peltola victory, but those claims have never been substantiated.

“It’s a disgrace,” Trump said.

data.title: GOP lawmaker says he will move to expel Omar
data.description:
Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) said Friday that he plans to introduce a resolution to expel Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) if a federal investigation finds she broke the law.

The Florida Republican is a conservative firebrand sometimes known for his past controversial comments, including describing Omar as a “terrorist” in 2025, a comment which House Democrats condemned as racist. 

Fine told The Hill’s broadcast partner NewsNation that he had already reached out to the Department of Justice (DOJ) to ask for more details on the investigation into Omar.

Omar’s Washington home was raided by federal immigration authorities Oct. 12 as part of a criminal investigation into her immigration status. Born in Somalia, Omar became a U.S. citizen in 2000 after her father was naturalized, but some on the right have long accused the Minnesota congresswoman of marrying her brother in order to obtain citizenship. Omar has repeatedly denied those claims.

The DOJ typically does not pursue law enforcement actions against political candidates this close to an election. Omar is running for reelection in this year’s midterms.

Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked about the timing of the investigation Thursday as he was announcing an indictment against another Democratic lawmaker: Virginia state Sen. Louise Lucas (D).

“This is a long-running case, as alleged in the indictment,” Blanche said. “People can criticize all they want, but it was time to bring the charges. The grand jury returned an indictment, and we made the arrests.”

President Trump said Thursday that Omar should resign “immediately,” accusing her of having a fake name.

“Because she used a fake name to be sworn in, I assume she must IMMEDIATELY resign from Congress,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “Please inform the Speaker of the House of Representatives, James Michael Johnson, that the Dumocrat Party has just conceded her seat.”

Omar said in a statement to NewsNation Friday that accusations that she has a fake name are “categorically false” and have “no basis in fact.”

As one of the most progressive members of the House, Omar has been a target of Trump and Republicans for years.

In 2019, Trump tweeted that Omar, along with Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.) and Ayanna Pressley (D-Mass.) should “go back” to where they came from, though Omar was the only one of the four who was not born in the U.S.

“Why don’t they go back and help fix the totally broken and crime infested places from which they came,” Trump wrote at the time.

The House voted to condemn Trump’s language as “racist” 240 to 187, with four Republicans voting with Democrats.

data.title: Ketanji Brown Jackson issues public dissent in New Hampshire voting case
data.description:
Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson publicly broke with her Supreme Court colleagues in a Thursday ruling allowing New Hampshire to fully block voters from using student IDs in the upcoming midterms.

Jackson, the high court’s most junior liberal justice, wrote in a short dissent that she would have left in place a lower court decision that found New Hampshire’s Republican secretary of state went too far with the voter identification restriction.

“I respectfully dissent because—even, and perhaps especially, when an election is looming—I would not disturb a clearly justifiable federal-court order issued to ensure that the public receives accurate information about a State’s electoral processes,” Jackson wrote.

None of the other justices publicly indicated their votes, which is common for cases decided on the court’s emergency docket. It is also not unusual for Jackson to dissent on her own.

The case stemmed from a law passed by the Republican-controlled state legislature earlier this year that prohibited student identification cards from being used to register to vote or receive a ballot for the Nov. 3 election.

Voting advocacy groups sued, arguing the restrictions were unconstitutional and discriminated against young voters.

U.S. District Judge Joseph Laplante declined to block the law entirely but ruled the plaintiffs were likely to succeed in their claim that the secretary of state’s directive went further than the statute itself. He said the state still needed to consider student IDs as evidence of voter identity.

The Supreme Court sided with New Hampshire, citing a longstanding legal principle known as Purcell, which says courts should not intervene to alter the rules so close to an election to avoid voter confusion.  

“Here, the District Court did not point to anything that would justify deviating from that principle,” the majority wrote in its brief, unsigned opinion.

Jackson argued Purcell did not apply in this case because the judge’s injunction was “reasonably designed to address alleged misinformation, not to change the law.”

“Under such circumstances, the relief the District Court provided actually promoted the interests Purcell sought to protect,” the justice wrote. “When a federal court determines that material misrepresentations are being made about a State’s election rules, an injunction to prohibit that conduct does not contribute to public confusion, it prevents that very problem.”

The Senate race in New Hampshire is shaping up to be one that could help decide control of the upper chamber, with Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas running against former Republican Sen. John Sununu. The Hill’s election forecasting partner, Decision Desk HQ, ranks the race as a “likely” victory for the Democrat.

data.title: Nationwide recall on these compound GLP-1 drugs
data.description:
(NewsNation) — The FDA has issued a recall for 23 GLP-1 compounded vials from Apothecary Pharma LLC due to lack of assurance the vials are sterile.

The FDA has designated the recall as Class II, meaning exposure to the products could cause reversible or temporary health consequences and poses little risk of serious consequences from use, according to the FDA website.

What products to look out for:

The recall applies to 22 vials of Tirzepatide Injection, 18mg/mL, 4 mL Sterile Multi-Dose Vial, Rx only, Apothecary Pharma, LLC, 1913 Evans Road, Cary, NC 27513, NDC 85091-001-18. Tirzepatide is used in Zepbound and Mounjaro. Customers should look out for these specific codes:

  • Lot AP-202622, BUD 07-Oct-2026
  • Lot AP-202623, BUD 08-Oct-2026
  • Lot AP-202624, BUD 19-Oct-2026
  • Lot AP-202625, BUD 10/20/2026
  • Lot AP-202627, BUD 10/26/2026
  • Lot AP-202628, BUD 10/27/2026
  • Lot AP-202629, BUD 10/28/2026
  • Lot AP-202630, BUD 10/31/2026
  • Lot AP-202631, BUD 11/01/2026
  • Lot AP-202632, BUD 11/03/2026
  • Lot AP-202633, BUD 11/07/2026
  • Lot AP-202634, BUD 11/08/2026
  • Lot AP-202635, BUD 11/16/2026
  • Lot AP-202636, BUD 11/17/2026
  • Lot AP-202637,BUD 11/18/2026
  • Lot AP-202638, BUD 11/19/2026

  • Lot AP-202641, BUD 11/22/2026
  • Lot AP-202642, BUD 11/24/2026
  • Lot AP-202643, BUD 11/25/2026
  • Lot AP-202644, BUD 11/26/2026

The recall also applies to one vial of NAD+ Injection 200 mg/mL, 6 mL Sterile Multi-Dose Vial, Rx Only, Apothecary Pharma, LLC, 1913 Evans Road, Cary, NC, 27513, NDC 85091-011-06. The code information is: Lot #: AP-202647, BUD 13-Oct-2026

Compounding pharmacy flagged by the FDA before

Apothecary Pharma in December 2025 received a letter from the FDA stating, “FDA investigators noted that drug products intended or expected to be sterile were prepared, packed, or held under insanitary conditions, whereby they may have become contaminated with filth or rendered injurious to health, causing your drug products to be adulterated under section 501(a)(2)(A) of the FDCA.”

What are compounding pharmacies?

Apothecary Pharma LLC is a compounding pharmacy in North Carolina. Compounded GLP-1s are not FDA-approved or name-brand. These pharmacies create customized versions of drugs for patients rather than mass-producing them like a commercial pharmacy, and they can adjust medications and create new versions to meet the patient’s specific needs

Although these pharmacies use FDA-approved ingredients, the products themselves are not checked for effectiveness, safety or purity, according to an article in Harvard Health Publishing. The FDA occasionally grants these pharmacies permission to produce drugs in bulk during shortages. In 2022, compounders were given permission to produce their own GLP-1 drugs to fill a shortage at the time. However, tirzepatide and semaglutide were removed from the drug shortage list in late 2024 and early 2025, according to Pharmacy Times reporting. Compound pharmacies continue to produce GLP-1s despite the lack of a shortage.

The FDA has not released official instructions on what to do if you discover you purchased a recalled vial; no illnesses have been linked to the recall at this time. Consumers should stop using it and contact their healthcare provider for guidance.

data.title: Vance becomes a hurricane as it nears Mexico
data.description:
Hurricane Vance is expected to steadily intensify in the next 24 hours and turn into a major hurricane by Friday night, according to the projections of the National Hurricane Center.

“Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this weekend and continue into next week,” the hurricane center said in an advisory Friday morning.

“These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions,” the advisory said.

Vance, which became a hurricane Friday, was a Category 1 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph and could become a major Category 3 hurricane before the end of Friday, the Associated Press reported.

It could be the seventh major hurricane in a row this year in the Pacific Ocean, following Nolo, Odalys, Polo, Rachel, Simon and Trudy.

The northeastern and central Pacific basins saw a number of powerful storms this year with at least 20 named storms in the region by Sept. 28, according to a NASA report. Nine of those storms had reached hurricane strength.

The intense hurricane season in the Pacific comes as El Nino conditions create unusual weather patterns.

In July, the AP reported that this year’s El Nino had an 81 percent chance of becoming “very strong” by fall, altering weather patterns across the globe.

data.title: Appeals court rules Trump unlawfully deployed National Guard to California
data.description:
A federal appeals court on Friday ruled 2-1 that President Trump’s National Guard deployment to the Los Angeles area last year was unlawful. 

The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit rejected Trump’s assertion that violent demonstrations in the city protesting his immigration crackdown justified him to wrest control of the troops from Gov. Gavin Newsom (D). 

Though Trump’s deployment has ended, the decision caps a year of consideration by the appeals court. 

At an earlier stage of the case, the 9th Circuit sided with Trump. It’s now ruling against him after the Supreme Court similarly found Trump didn’t meet the legal requirements to unilaterally deploy the National Guard to Chicago.

“Defendants have not made either of the required threshold showings here. Thus, they have not carried their burden,” U.S. Circuit Judge Jennifer Sung, an appointee of former President Biden. 

Sung was joined on the panel by two Trump-nominated judges, Eric Miller and Mark Bennett. Miller also sided against Trump, while Bennett dissented. 

Bennett said his colleagues shouldn’t have decided the case, as the administration wanted to dismiss the appeal and head back to the trial court to litigate the impact of the Supreme Court’s ruling.  

“But the majority insists on pressing forward, relying primarily on outdated briefs prepared amid a shifting legal landscape,” Bennett wrote. 

It means Friday’s decision will now bind future 9th Circuit panels if Trump tries to deploy the National Guard again in California. 

Last year, Trump deployed the National Guard to various blue cities around the country — including Washington, D.C., Memphis and Portland, Ore. — to quell protests against his immigration crackdown.  

In Los Angeles, the demonstrations devolved into violence at times, with reports of looting and some having thrown Molotov cocktails.

The president deployed the National Guard by invoking a law allowing him to federalize troops whenever there is a rebellion or when he cannot execute the law with regular forces. 

The Supreme Court last year said Trump hadn’t met the criteria because “regular forces” likely refers to the U.S. military.

Trump’s National Guard deployment in the nation’s capital, which relies on a different legal authority, remains ongoing.

data.title: Meghan Markle says she's 'deeply distressed' in response to child pornography allegations against her father
data.description:
Meghan Markle has addressed the accusations against her father, who is being investigated over alleged possession of child sexual abuse material.

Markle, Duchess of Sussex and wife to Great Britain’s Prince Harry, said she was “deeply distressed” by the news on 82-year-old Thomas Markle Sr. that has spread through tabloids in recent days. Markle and her family recently returned to England after forfeiting their royal duties and living in the United States for a number of years.

“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” Markle wrote in a statement obtained by The Hill. 

According to British tabloid The Sun, Markle’s half-brother Thomas Markle Jr. told police he found “hundreds if not thousands” of child sexual abuse images in his father’s home. Markle, who is said to be estranged from her father for years, said allegations were made to British police in 2018 and were later shared with her. 

“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection,” Markle wrote. “That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.”

The Sun reported that Markle Jr. reported his father to officials after finding the boxes of photos and a 15-minute video of naked young girls on his father’s phone. Markle Jr. reported his father to multiple law enforcement authorities, including the FBI, The Sun reported. 

The Duchess said in her statement that she trusted the authorities to protect any families at risk while she avoided her father to protect her young children.

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” Markle wrote. “I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.”

Markle said she hopes that justice will be served and children will be protected.

“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” Markle wrote.

data.title: Ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden probe
data.description:
Two former Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) officials are facing charges for lying to Congress about their involvement in the agency’s investigation into Hunter Biden’s laptop.

Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, who worked in FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF) in 2019 and 2020, were taken into custody Friday, said FBI Director Kash Patel in a post on the social platform X.

Patel said in his post that both Floris and Benavides testified earlier that the FITF was not involved in the investigations into Biden, but documentary evidence, communications and witness accounts contradict their testimony.

“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system,” Patel said. “No one is above the law.”

Biden’s laptop was seized by the FBI in 2019 and contained some of his personal information. The contents of the laptop, including emails showing discussions of Biden’s foreign business dealings, were published by the New York Post, which said it had obtained a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Biden at a Delaware repair shop, according to the Associated Press.

In a Friday release, the Department of Justice (DOJ) said the charges stem from an ongoing investigation into the FTIF.

The department cited evidence that Floris discussed the FBI’s investigations routinely for more than a year within the FITF and with others in the FBI. Benavides also regularly discussed the laptop investigation with FBI officials.

“The weaponization of government goes against the interest of the American people, and public servants, including federal law enforcement officials, cannot lie to Congress and get away with it,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said in the DOJ release.

Both Floris and Benavides made their first appearance in federal court in Washington following their surrender Friday, where their lawyers asked for a speedy hearing at which they could contest the allegations, the AP reported.

Floris’s lawyers issued a statement disputing the allegations and calling her “a patriot.”

“Nikki Floris is a patriot. She served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years,” a statement obtained by The Hill said.

“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election,” the statement continued.
